array.caption.append: Laid it on the end — nothing had to shift
array.caption.base: An array packs equal-width cells side by side with no gaps and calls each one by a number counted from 0 — know the number and you arrive in one step, but touch the middle and the neighbours shift along.
array.caption.handover: Your turn — type an index and a value, then press Read, Write, Insert, Remove, Append or Search.
array.caption.insert: Slid one in at {index} — the {shifted} cells behind it each moved one place along
array.caption.limitReached: Reached the teaching limit of {maxSize} — no further {op} is possible
array.caption.outOfRange: That position is out of range ({op} {index}) — nothing happens on the strip
array.caption.read: Jumped straight to cell {index} — one "start + {index}" reaches {value}
array.caption.remove: Emptied {index} — the {shifted} cells behind it each pulled one place back
array.caption.resize: The cells are full — moving {copied} of them onto a new strip twice the size
array.caption.searchMiss: Not found — scanned the whole strip
array.caption.write: Replaced the value in cell {index} — the neighbours are untouched
cachingCdn.caption.base: A CDN is the system-level behaviour of edges worldwide taking requests from nearby clients — answering short when they hold the answer, and travelling up the hierarchy to fetch and keep it when they do not.
cachingCdn.caption.coldStart: Every edge on the map is grey — starting from an empty cache.
cachingCdn.caption.handover: Your turn — type a content name and an edge, then press Request, Demo or Reset.
cachingCdn.caption.hit: Answered right at the {edge} edge — one short round trip ({detail}).
cachingCdn.caption.missOrigin: {edge} missed — went all the way to the origin and filled the edge on the way back ({detail}).
cachingCdn.caption.missRegional: {edge} missed — caught at the regional cache, so the origin was never reached ({detail}).
cachingCdn.caption.purge: Invalidated the {edge} edge — the next request travels up the hierarchy again.
cachingCdn.label.references: See also: Cloudflare CDN Reference Architecture · Cloudflare Global Network · ByteByteGo CDN · NAVER Cloud CDN tips
cachingCdn.legend.hitMiss: A hit is one short arc from client to edge — a miss is the long trip up the hierarchy and back, filling the edge on the way.
conditionalStatement.caption.base: A conditional is the promise that when running code reaches a fork it reads whether the current value is true or false, passes through exactly one branch, and then gathers back into a single line.
contextSwitching.caption.base: Context switching — on a single CPU stage one flow's whole register set is lifted out into its own holder, the other flow's set is placed back into those same slots, and each resumes exactly where it stopped.
contextSwitching.caption.holderThicker: The holders got thicker — there is more to carry across.
contextSwitching.caption.holderThinner: The holders got thinner — two threads inside one process.
contextSwitching.caption.restore: Placing the next flow's state back onto the stage.
contextSwitching.caption.resume: Carrying on — it resumes exactly where it stopped.
contextSwitching.caption.save: Lifting the current state out into the holder.
contextSwitching.caption.stageEmpty: The stage is empty — nobody is making progress.
contextSwitching.caption.triggerArrived: A trigger arrived — the flow stops.
contextSwitching.concept.line1: Context switching — on a single CPU stage one flow's whole register set is lifted out into its own holder,
contextSwitching.concept.line2: and the other flow's set is placed back into those same slots, so each resumes exactly where it stopped.
contextSwitching.label.aria: Context switching visualization — one CPU stage, holders on each side, triggers from the ceiling, and a time strip
contextSwitching.label.ceiling: — ceiling: where triggers come down from outside —
contextSwitching.label.references: See also — OSTEP · Silberschatz · Wikipedia · Process Scheduling Visualizer
contextSwitching.label.timeStrip: time strip — flow colour = progress, grey hatching = empty time (overhead)
contextSwitching.label.title: Context switching — stage / holders / time
hashTableChaining.caption.alphaWarn: The table is getting cramped — it will need to grow soon.
hashTableChaining.caption.base: A hash table lays out a row of identical slots and a function box throws each key into the one slot it picks — when two land on the same slot, a chain grows there.
hashTableChaining.caption.collision: Two landed on the same slot — the chain grows by one.
hashTableChaining.caption.duplicate: key {key} is already on that chain.
hashTableChaining.caption.emptyTableOp: The table is empty — there is no key to search for or remove.
hashTableChaining.caption.handover: Your turn — type a key, then press Insert, Search or Remove.
hashTableChaining.caption.insert: Threw the key into the slot the function chose.
hashTableChaining.caption.rehashBegin: The table got cramped — growing it and throwing everything again.
hashTableChaining.caption.rehashEnd: Grew the table and threw everything again — α is back in the safe range.
hashTableChaining.caption.removeStart: The function box points at a slot — taking it off there.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchFound: One jump plus {walked} comparisons — arrived at {key} in index {index}.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchMiss: That key is not on this slot's chain.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchStart: The function box points at a slot — now walking that slot's chain.
hashTableChaining.label.auxProbingNote: it squeezes sideways and moves on
hashTableChaining.label.auxRehashNote: the main view shows the new table, the side panel the old one
linearRegression.caption.base: Linear regression threads one straight line through a cloud of points, turning each residual into the area of a square, and nudges the line a step at a time so the total of those areas shrinks.
linearRegression.caption.converged: Converged — it will not shrink any further.
linearRegression.caption.diverged: The learning rate is too large — the line diverged.
linearRegression.concept.line1: Linear regression threads one line through a cloud of points,
linearRegression.concept.line2: turning each residual into an area and rotating and shifting the line
linearRegression.concept.line3: one step per iteration so those areas add up to as little as possible.
linearRegression.label.aria: Linear regression visualization — residual squares synchronized one-to-one with the contour map
linearRegression.label.lossCurve: loss curve — RSS over time t
linearRegression.label.references: See also — Setosa · ml-visualized · Google ML Crash Course · angeloyeo
linearRegression.label.title: Linear regression — as the residual areas shrink, the dot rolls down into the valley
linkedListSingly.caption.base: In a linked list every node holds a single finger pointing only at its own next — inserting or removing is not moving cards around but cutting and retying two or three fingers.
linkedListSingly.caption.handover: Your turn — type an index and a value, then press Insert, Remove or Search.
linkedListSingly.caption.headSlideNew: The head label glided over to the new card.
linkedListSingly.caption.headSlideSecond: The head label glided over to the second card.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertBindNext: Tied the new card's finger to the next card first.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertHeadBind: Tied the new card's finger to the old first card.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertLimit: Reached the teaching limit — no more cards can be threaded in.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertRewirePre: Moved the previous card's finger over to the new card.
linkedListSingly.caption.removeRewire: Moved the previous card's finger straight on to the next card.
linkedListSingly.caption.searchFound: Found it after {walked} steps — {value} at index {index}
linkedListSingly.caption.searchMiss: Walked to the end, and that value was not there.
linkedListSingly.caption.searchStart: Starting at the head — following the fingers one step at a time.
lruCache.caption.base: An LRU cache shares one set of nodes between a hash map (key → node) and a doubly linked list (recency order) — every call drags a node to the MRU end, and on overflow the LRU end vanishes from both areas at once.
lruCache.caption.evict: Over capacity — {key} at the LRU end disappears from both areas together.
lruCache.caption.getHit: {key} was dragged to the MRU end — even a get rotates the list.
lruCache.caption.getMiss: {key} is not in the cache — the list stays as it was.
lruCache.caption.handover: Your turn — type a key and value, then press get or put.
lruCache.caption.invalidKey: {op}: only short alphanumeric keys (values) are accepted — got "{raw}"
lruCache.caption.putInsert: New key {key} entered at the MRU end (room to spare).
lruCache.caption.putUpdate: The value for {key} was updated and dragged to the MRU end.
lruCache.label.references: See also: NeetCode 146 · dev.to LRU illustrated · GeeksforGeeks LRU
lruCache.narrative.line1: An LRU cache carves a "recency order" onto a plain key-value store.
lruCache.narrative.line2: The hash slots on top give fast key → node pointer lookup,
lruCache.narrative.line3: while the doubly linked list below carries the order of use.
lruCache.narrative.line4: Both areas share the same nodes, so every call updates the two at once.
lruCache.narrative.line5: Even a get is a write in effect — it drags its node to the MRU end.
lruCache.narrative.line6: A put on a full cache makes the node at the LRU end vanish from both areas together.
messagingPubsub.caption.base: Pub/Sub lets publishers and subscribers know only the broker's topic label instead of each other's identity — one publish fans out to every subscriber as copies, making many-to-many asynchronous messaging work.
messagingPubsub.caption.handover: Your turn — type a publisher, topic and subscriber, then press publish, subscribe or unsubscribe.
messagingPubsub.caption.publishFanout: One publish → {count} copies → each arriving at its own moment ({topic}).
messagingPubsub.caption.publishNoSubscri: {publisher} → {topic} published — nobody is listening on that topic.
messagingPubsub.caption.subscribe: {subscriber} joined {topic} — earlier publishes do not reach it.
messagingPubsub.caption.unsubscribe: {subscriber} left {topic} — later publishes will not reach it.
messagingPubsub.label.references: See also: Hohpe — Publish-Subscribe Channel · MS Azure Architecture Center · GoF Observer · Aiven Kafka Visualization
messagingPubsub.legend.indirection: Publishers throw only at a topic and subscribers ask only for a topic — the broker in between hands out the copies, and every arrow breaks once at the broker lifeline and starts again.
stack.caption.base: A stack hands back the most recently added element first — every change happens at one single place, the top.
stack.caption.feedInput: Boxes are waiting on the input track — they will be stacked on top one by one.
stack.caption.handover: Your turn — type a value and press Push, Pop or Peek.
stack.caption.peek: Looked at the top value — the pile is unchanged.
stack.caption.push: Placed a new box on top — {value}
stack.caption.underflow: No box left to take off.
tokenization.caption.base: Tokenization is the first stage of a compiler. It reads the source a character at a time from left to right and cuts it into the smallest units that carry meaning — taking the longest run it can, and leaving whitespace and comments as nothing but traces.
tokenization.caption.comment: A comment never becomes a token — it stays as a trace.
tokenization.caption.unrecognized: An unrecognized character — it lands as a red card.
tokenization.concept.line1: Tokenization is the first stage of a compiler — reading left to right, one
tokenization.concept.line2: character at a time, it cuts the source into the smallest meaningful units
tokenization.concept.line3: (tokens), taking the longest run it can. Whitespace and comments never
tokenization.concept.line4: become tokens and sink into grey. Watch the strip above feed the cards below.
tokenization.label.title: Tokenization — one beat of condensation
